title: Windows 11 Preview Adds Search Tools and Menu Customization
summary: Microsoft's latest Windows 11 Release Preview updates introduce enhanced Search capabilities and customizable right-click context menus across different OS
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Microsoft rolled out Windows 11 Release Preview updates on November 15, 2026, enhancing Search and right-click menus.
- New Search features include expanded task automation while context menus gain granular customization controls across versions.
- Updates deploy gradually across Windows 11 22H2, 23H2, and 24H2 builds through the Release Preview channel.


Microsoft has officially released new Windows 11 preview updates through its Release Preview channel, introducing enhanced Search capabilities and expanded right-click context menu customization. Officially launched on November 15, 2026, these updates roll out incrementally across multiple Windows 11 versions, giving users more control over interface elements and task automation.


## Enhanced Search Functionality


The updated Search experience assigns additional automation tasks to Windows Search, expanding its role beyond simple file and web queries. Users can now trigger system-level actions directly from the Search interface, streamlining common workflows without navigating through Settings menus or Control Panel dialogs.


According to Microsoft's release notes, the Search enhancements integrate with Windows 11's existing quick actions framework. This allows users to execute tasks like network troubleshooting, storage cleanup, and accessibility adjustments through natural language queries. The feature leverages local indexing to provide instant results without requiring cloud connectivity.


## Customizable Right-Click Context Menus


The context menu updates introduce granular customization options, addressing long-standing user requests for more control over right-click interfaces. Windows 11 users can now add, remove, or reorder context menu items through a new Settings panel, eliminating clutter from third-party application entries.


Key customization features include:


- Per-file-type menu configurations for documents, images, and executables
- Quick toggle switches to hide legacy menu items
- Drag-and-drop reordering of menu entries
- Import and export menu layout profiles


The changes apply to File Explorer, Desktop, and Start menu contexts, maintaining consistency across the operating system interface.


## Gradual Rollout Across Windows 11 Versions


Microsoft is deploying these updates in stages across Windows 11 22H2, 23H2, and 24H2 builds. Users enrolled in the Release Preview channel receive updates first, with general availability expected to follow within weeks. The staggered approach allows Microsoft to monitor feedback and address compatibility issues before broader deployment.


Version-specific differences exist: Windows 11 24H2 receives the full feature set immediately, while 22H2 and 23H2 builds gain features through cumulative updates over the next month. Enterprise and Education editions can control feature deployment through Group Policy settings.


## Release Date and Availability


The updates were officially released on November 15, 2026, through Windows Update for devices enrolled in the Release Preview channel. Users can verify enrollment status in Settings under Windows Update > Windows Insider Program. Non-Insider users will receive these features automatically through standard monthly updates beginning in December 2026.


## What This Means


These incremental improvements reflect Microsoft's ongoing effort to refine Windows 11's user interface based on community feedback. The expanded Search capabilities reduce friction for common tasks, while context menu customization addresses a frequent pain point for power users managing multiple applications. By splitting features across versions and channels, Microsoft balances innovation with stability, ensuring enterprise environments can adopt changes at their own pace while consumer users gain immediate access to productivity enhancements.
